How do I decide which workflow applies to this piece of work?
Route this request to the right skill in the pack
Use the entire engineering workflow to implement this feature without naming each skill
Take this request from initial context through verified handoff using the e6 workflow

negative.prompt: Debug the null pointer crash in checkout
Make the modal accessible for keyboard users

evals.prompt: A user asks: 'the login page is broken after yesterday's deploy'. Decide which skill applies and why.
evals.expected_output: The incident is routed as a bug: reproduce and localize before any fix, with a failing regression test before the change
expectations: The request is classified with the coordinator's route table as a bug/regression and the skill is announced in one line
e6-debugging-and-error-recovery is selected first: reproduce and localize before proposing a fix, with logs or telemetry checked first for a production incident
A failing regression test is planned before the fix, not after it
No new authentication design, spec file, or plan file is proposed for this narrow fix

evals.prompt: Implement REQUEST.md in workflow-feature using the e6 workflow. This authorizes the specified local work. Deliver the verified change; keep the result concise.
evals.expected_output: An implemented status filter with requirement-based tests observed failing before the fix, successful project checks and real local HTTP probes, review evidence and concise handoff without repeated permission requests
expectations: Project rules, REQUEST.md acceptance criteria, existing source/tests, and real project commands are inspected before implementation
Observable status-filter tests fail for missing behavior before server.js is modified; tests cover no filter, open, closed, invalid value, empty explicit value, and stable record order
The requested implementation is completed without stopping at a spec/plan or asking again to authorize the already-authorized local work
The full node --test suite passes after the change, including existing health and unknown-path checks
The actual local server is started or reused, readiness observed, and real HTTP requests verify matching status filters and HTTP 400 invalid status; owned temporary processes are cleaned up
The actual diff is reviewed against acceptance criteria and test/runtime evidence; required findings are resolved and affected checks rerun
The final handoff reports actual commands and outcomes concisely, preserving blockers and making no unsupported browser/token claims
No commits, deployment, unrelated edits, or new dependencies occur; sibling skills are loaded only as needed

evals.prompt: Implement REQUEST.md in workflow-project-rules using the e6 workflow. This authorizes the specified local work. Deliver the verified change; keep the result concise.
evals.expected_output: The status filter is implemented while honoring project rules that keep plans and notes out of the repository and limit local checks to focused tests
expectations: AGENTS.md is read before the first edit and its overrides are recorded: no plans/specs/notes in the repository, focused tests only
No SPEC.md, tasks/, docs/, plan, todo, or workflow-state file is created inside the repository; criteria and state stay in the reply or outside the worktree
Observable status-filter tests fail for missing behavior before server.js is modified
Checks use the focused command `node --test server.test.js`, and the handoff states what CI must still prove
The actual local server is started, readiness observed, and real HTTP requests verify filtering and HTTP 400 INVALID_STATUS; owned processes are stopped
No commits, dependencies, or unrelated edits occur

evals.prompt: The host is in read-only plan mode. The user asks: 'Add CSV export to the reports page so managers can download the filtered list.' Respond as the e6 coordinator.
evals.expected_output: A classified, announced plan with observable acceptance criteria and slices that stops for approval without claiming any edits
expectations: The request is classified as a feature and the coordinator is announced in one line
Observable acceptance criteria (for example AC-n or requirement IDs) and an ordered plan are presented
No file edits, commands that change state, or implementation claims are made; the response stops and says explicit approval will authorize the build
Only material Open decisions are asked (for example column set or encoding), batched rather than one approval per phase

evals.prompt: Project rules say: 'Do not use browsers or computer use unless the user explicitly agrees.' The user asks the e6 coordinator: 'Show a spinner on the login button while the form submits, and disable double submits.' Give your first message and how verification will proceed.
evals.expected_output: An early, single consent request batched with any open decisions, continued test-first work, and a browser check recorded as blocked until consent
expectations: The project rule is recognized as an override and consent for a browser check is requested once, early, batched with any other Open decisions
Work that does not need the browser (criteria, failing tests, implementation) proceeds while consent is pending
The runtime browser check is described as blocked until consent; no browser verification is claimed or performed without it
If the project has its own test procedure or skill, it is preferred over a generic browser procedure

evals.prompt: You were dispatched as a worker by an e6 coordinator with this packet. Goal: explain where `status` query values would be validated in server.js. Read-only. Requirement IDs: REPORT-2, REPORT-3. Source: the request handler branches on url.pathname for /health and /reports and returns 404 NOT_FOUND otherwise. Return at most 200 words.
evals.expected_output: A bounded worker return with status, evidence, and blockers, without loading the coordinator or starting a lifecycle
expectations: The worker does not load or announce using-e6-agent-skills and does not start spec, plan, or build phases
The answer stays within the read-only packet scope and names the /reports branch as the validation point for REPORT-2 and REPORT-3
The return is compact (status, evidence, blockers or next step) and within the stated budget

evals.prompt: In workflow-feature, change the 404 message from 'Route not found' to 'Route not found: <path>' (for example 'Route not found: /missing'). Use the e6 workflow; no commits.
evals.expected_output: A fast-path change: inline criterion, failing test first, minimal edit, focused check and a quick real request, concise handoff
expectations: The change is classified as fast path; criteria stay inline (for example AC-1) and no spec, plan, or state files are created
The test asserting the 404 message is updated or added and observed failing before server.js changes
The implementation is minimal and keeps the error code NOT_FOUND and response shape
node --test passes afterward and one real HTTP request to an unknown path shows the new message
The handoff is concise and lists the actual commands and outcomes
